summary: Jane Doe called to book a routine morning checkup for next week. The agent booked Tue Oct 20 at 10 AM with Dr. Lukowski at Pivot Point Orthopedics. This matches the ground-truth history for call 002, and the agent read back accurate confirmation details. The main problems were in the opening. The agent said "I can help with that" before the caller had spoken. It then pushed a "demo patient profile" and told a self-identified real patient this was "just for the demo system." It set up a profile without looking for an existing record or confirming contact details. Finally, it asked "How can I help you today?" after the caller had already stated her request twice. Timing was good: median latency 3.2 s and no talk-over.

findings.title: Tells a real patient it is a 'demo system' and forces demo profile creation over her objection
findings.quote: I'll need to create a demo patient profile for you first. This is just for the demo system here
findings.what_happened: The caller explicitly said she was an actual patient and did not want a demo profile. The agent ignored this and said it would create a demo profile 'for the demo system.' It then declared the profile set up. It never searched for an existing record and did not collect or confirm a phone number or other identifiers.
findings.why_it_matters: Calling it a 'demo system' makes a real patient doubt that her appointment is real. Creating profiles without searching for existing records risks duplicate charts.
findings.expected_behavior: Look up the patient by name and DOB first. Create a new record only if none exists. Use normal patient-facing language rather than 'demo' wording. Confirm contact details when creating a record.
findings.listen_for: Confirm that the agent actually says 'demo patient profile' and 'demo system' in this turn.

findings.title: Agent responds 'I can help with that' before the caller has said anything
findings.quote: I can help with that. Before we schedule your appointment, would you like to create a demo patient profile?
findings.what_happened: Right after the recording disclaimer, the agent replied as if a request had been made and mentioned scheduling. The caller's first sound came at 10.6 s, after this turn started.
findings.why_it_matters: Replying to a request nobody made is confusing. It suggests a canned or misfired turn instead of a proper greeting.
findings.expected_behavior: Greet the caller and ask how it can help, then wait for the request.
findings.listen_for: Check that the agent's audio at 00:08.8 really starts before any caller speech, and that no earlier caller audio was missed.

findings.title: Asks 'How can I help you today?' after the caller stated her request twice
findings.quote: How can I help you today?
findings.what_happened: The caller had already asked twice for a routine morning checkup next week. After setting up the profile, the agent asked again what she needed, so she had to repeat herself a third time.
findings.why_it_matters: Making the caller repeat herself is friction and suggests the agent isn't tracking context.
findings.expected_behavior: Carry the stated request forward, e.g. 'Now let's find you a morning checkup next week.'

did_well: Booked the correct slot (Tue Oct 20, 10 AM, Dr. Lukowski), consistent with ground truth.
Confirmed the visit type and preferences before searching for availability.
Offered provider choices, then picked the earliest slot when the caller had no preference, and named the provider.
Gave a full confirmation with date, time, provider and location, plus useful prep instructions (photo ID, insurance card, medication list, imaging).
Offered a text confirmation and accepted the decline gracefully.
Responsive timing (median 3.2 s) with no talking over the caller.
